name: Agneeswarar Temple, Tirukkollikadu
deity: Shiva as Agneeswarar, with the goddess Panjin Melladi Ammai (Mridupada Nayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirukkollikadu, near Thiruthuraipoondi in the lower Tiruvarur delta, honours Shiva as Agneeswarar with the goddess Panjin Melladi Ammai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar — the 115th shrine of the Kaveri's southern bank — it is bound to the worship of Agni, the fire-god, from which the lord takes his name.

sections.history: Tirukkollikadu lies about 18 km from Thiruthuraipoondi (and some 18–25 km from Tiruvarur), in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam (No. 115 on the southern bank of the Kaveri), hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, keeping the form of the Shiva shrines of the lower delta.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Agneeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Panjin Melladi Ammai — 'she of feet soft as cotton,' also named Mridupada Nayaki — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram keep the form of the Shiva temples of the lower Tiruvarur delta.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Agneeswarar, 'the lord of Agni,' from the worship offered by Agni, the fire-god, who by tradition did penance here; the lord's name recalls that devotion. The goddess is Panjin Melladi Ammai, whose feet are soft as cotton (panju). As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims of the Thiruthuraipoondi tract include Tirukkollikadu among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirukkollikadu the pilgrim comes to the lord of the fire-god's worship. Before Agneeswarar and Panjin Melladi Ammai, in the lower Tiruvarur delta, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple, firm in the devotion of Agni that gives the lord his name.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkollikadu lies about 18 km from Thiruthuraipoondi in Tiruvarur district. Thiruthuraipoondi and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
